correctness.rationale: The proof constructs a bijection between cyclic de Bruijn 32-cycles and binary four-input feedback truth tables whose 32-state permutation consists of one cycle. Each length-six factor is determined by a state; a reverse factor occurs exactly for matching feedback of reversed four-bit suffixes. Nonpalindromic suffix pairs each save two reversal classes, palindromic suffixes with feedback 1 save one, giving r(6)=28-2A+Z; all cycles have r(5)=20. A separate independent DFS enumerated all 2048 rooted directed Hamiltonian cycles and found the exact spectrum r(6):22/576, 25/960, 26/192, 28/256, 29/64. The finite exhaustive domain is all 2^16 tables, not a sample. No general order-six spectrum asserted.

evidence: Allouche et al supply general complexity identities, not the distribution of order-five feedback maps; Chang–Wang restrict to special symmetry classes.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General reflection formulas do not determine a distribution across 2048 specific finite cycles without exhaustive feedback classifications; symmetry counts are not a stronger implication.

originality.rationale: The new object is a census of reversal-orbit factor counts across every order-five binary cyclic de Bruijn word. Allouche et al establish reflection complexity and general factor/palindrome identities; Chang–Wang study global reverse-complement symmetric cycles, a different equivalence and statistic. Neither inspected primary statement tabulates the five exact classes or the joint (A,Z) distribution. The classical total 2048 is prior and not itself the new result; independent semantic searches did not locate a dominating exact table.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed special-purpose exact reflection-complexity census could duplicate the five-bin table.
Finite exhaustive result for order five must not be extrapolated to higher orders.
